Olga,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We are ready to start sizing out dedicated capacity for our clinical summarization product. High level profile below and a couple of asks — can you and your team confirm the SKU recommendations and a preliminary capacity map we can put in our internal roadmap? We9d like a clear fallthrough plan if demand spikes.

Workload snapshot (approx):
- Peak concurrent requests: 220
- Typical traffic: 90-120 qps sustained with burst to 350 qps for 10-15 minutes
- Average prompt + generation: 450 tokens (mostly short), but 8% of calls require long-context summarization up to 32k tokens
- Latency SLO: 99p < 250ms for short requests, 99p < 1s for long-context summaries
- Model: fine-tuned open-llm-34B variant; memory-sensitive KV cache needs for long-context runs
- Budget: constrained; procurement prefers reserved capacity but needs cost/latency tradeoffs

Attachments: I attached our exported workload CSV and a spreadsheet with peak windows.

Could you provide: 
1) Recommended SKU mix (H100 / A100 / L4) with rationale for fallthroughs
2) A simple ops guidance (cache + tiling suggestions) we can hand to our infra team
3) Any questions from a procurement perspective (DocuSign, lead times)

Best,
Zara Malik

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing for Proxima - workload summary and ask

Hi Zara — thanks for the detailed profile and CSV. Quick summary up front: we recommend a mixed pool approach with reserved H100 capacity specifically for the long-context workload, A100s for the bulk throughput with predictable latency, and a small L4 pool for cost-sensitive, low-memory endpoints. I9ve attached a compact tradeoff matrix and a first-pass capacity map.

High-level SKU rationale (short):
- H100 (reserved): best for 32k context runs because of large HBM and stronger sustained memory bandwidth — reduces KV cache pressure and avoids frequent tiling. Use for the 8% long-context tier. Plan: reserve enough H100 slots to cover ~40 concurrent long-context sessions (headroom for spikes).
- A100 (reserved + burstable): cost-effective for throughput; good for most generation workloads up to ~16k contexts when we employ prefix tiling + KV caching. Plan: majority of baseline capacity here, autoscale with burst credits to handle spikes.
- L4 (on Dedicated or burst pools): excellent unit economics for short prompts/embeddings when latency is primary and memory need is small. Not suitable for 32k runs. Use as low-cost fallback for non-critical endpoints and for developer sandboxing.

Specifics proposed (first pass):
- Target steady-state slots: H100 x 20 slots (reserve), A100 x 60 slots (reserve), L4 x 10 slots (reserve)
- Burst plan: A100 burst pool + shared L4 on-demand. H100 burst only if agreed to higher commit or multi-cloud fallback (we can run short-burst long-context on A100 with tiling but at higher latency).
- Cost/latency expectations: short requests on A100/L4 should meet your 99p < 250ms target if batching kept shallow and KV cache hot; long-context on H100 targets ~700-900ms 99p depending on model sequence length distribution.

Ops/tiling suggestions (brief):
- KV prefix caching for repeated patient context across calls (cache eviction policy tuned for session length > 8k)
- Aggressive request routing: long-context routed to H100 cluster by policy; short requests to A100/L4 with quick path tokens
- Continuous batching: keep batch window <= 8ms for latency-sensitive endpoints; allow 20-30ms for throughput endpoints

Procurement items: lead time on reserved H100 slots is ~8-10 weeks for capacity procurement and allocation; DocuSign template and pricing worksheet attached.

Next steps I9ll take: 1) loop in Dev/Infra (cc9d) to validate exact slot counts and ops playbook, 2) deliver a Mutual Action Plan doc for your sign-off with timelines and milestones.

Attaching: sku_tradeoff_matrix_H100_A100_L4.xlsx, proxima_workload_profile_v1.csv, proxima_map_mutual_action_plan.docx

Thanks — feel free to flag anything I missed.

— Olga Petrov

Olga / Lauren — quick pass from infra ops:
- A100 sizing: with conservative batching (avg batch size 2.5) and the requested steady qps window, 60 A100 slots should cover ~110 sustained qps with 99p ~200-240ms for your short prompt profile. If they want tighter 99p < 150ms we recommend adding ~15 A100 slots or shifting ~25% of short traffic to L4 where it9s latency-optimal.
- H100 headroom: holding 20 reserved H100 slots gives safe concurrency for ~40 simultaneous long-context sessions if we prioritize preemptible tiling and session-aware KV caching; real-world tail latency will still be model-dependent but should fall in the 700-950ms range at 32k. If Proxima intends to run long-context at higher concurrency spikes, we should suggest multi-region fallback or expand reserved H100 commitment.
- Fallthroughs / contingency: we should propose an automatic downgrade policy — route long requests to A100 with async processing and a progress indicator if H100 capacity constrained, and use L4 only for non-long-context calls. Also recommend a 6-week procurement buffer for H100 reservation.

I9ll update the mutual action plan with these numbers and add a recommended canary schedule for rollout.

— Dev
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
